newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals mostly slip, palladium mixed.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals mostly slip, palladium mixed.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mostly lower on Friday, weighed down by the yen's firmer tone against the dollar, traders said. Palladium was mixed after recovering from early lows,
Gold futures ranged from five yen to nine yen per gram lower, with most-active benchmark February off seven yen at 1,401 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from six yen lower to nine yen up, with benchmark February up two yen at 613 yen.
"Trading in platinum group metals was quite buoyant, while gold and silver was quiet," one trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $348.20/50 per ounce at 0716 GMT, against $348.40/90 in New York on Thursday.

In the palladium futures market, private investors, who were selling earlier, started to cover their short positions late in the day after benchmark February palladium failed to break under the 600 yen level.

The focus in the platinum group metals market was still on whether Russia will resume platinum group metals exports, but market players were sceptical over a Russian official's comments that the Russian government may sign a decree next week outlining platinum group metal deliveries to Japan.
"We have seen similar comments repeatedly, and every time we were disappointed. We see any falls in spot palladium as a chance for bargain-hunting buying," an official of a bullion house said.

In gold and platinum futures, private investors were slightly on the selling side. "Trading in gold futures was sluggish, reflecting thin interest," one trader said. Open interest of gold futures has declined in recent days.
Benchmark February platinum settled down seven yen per gram at 1,477 yen. Benchmark February silver was off 1.0 yen at 196.0 yen per 10 grams.
